div.div: Potential telemetry evidence against governance-mapped CIM datamodels — control gaps, not compliance scores.

div.p: What this shows: Mapped controls per framework, stacked by evidence quality in the selected sample — strong (distinctive CIM fields), weak/shared-only, or no usable evidence.
Why it matters: Governance is not a single coverage percentage. This shows where telemetry may support mapped requirements versus where evidence is only shared fields or missing.

Read it as: Potential evidence gaps, not compliance. Strong means at least one mapped datamodel has fields uncommon across CIM models. Weak means only shared fields (e.g. dest/user) lit the mapping. Drill into Governance IN for control detail.

search.query: | fields datamodel evidence_strength matched_fields | append [ | inputlookup governance_datamodel_mapping_lookup | eval selected_framework=if(len("$framework_filter$")=0,"*","$framework_filter$") | eval selected_framework_wrapped="|" . selected_framework . "|" | where selected_framework="*" OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|*|%") OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|" . framework . "|%") | eval selected_dm=if(len("$datamodel_filter$")=0,"*","$datamodel_filter$") | eval selected_dm_wrapped="|" . selected_dm . "|" | where selected_dm="*" OR like(selected_dm_wrapped,"%|*|%") OR like(selected_dm_wrapped,"%|" . datamodel . "|%") | eval mapping_row=1 | fields framework control_reference capability datamodel mapping_row ] | eventstats values(evidence_strength) as evidence_strength by datamodel | where mapping_row=1 | eval evidence_strength=coalesce(evidence_strength,"none") | eval strength_rank=case(evidence_strength="strong",3,evidence_strength="weak",2,true(),1) | stats max(strength_rank) as best_rank by framework control_reference | eval control_evidence=case(best_rank=3,"Strong evidence",best_rank=2,"Weak / shared-only",true(),"No usable evidence") | chart count over framework by control_evidence | fillnull value=0 "Strong evidence" "Weak / shared-only" "No usable evidence" | table framework "Strong evidence" "Weak / shared-only" "No usable evidence" | sort framework

Why it matters: Shows how much of the governance map has distinctive telemetry evidence versus shared-field noise or gaps.
Read it as: Potential evidence mix only — not compliance status or control effectiveness.

div.p: What this shows: Per-framework counts of mapped controls with strong, weak/shared-only, or no usable telemetry evidence.
Why it matters: Connects the stacked gap view to control and datamodel counts for drill-down.
Read it as: Potential evidence summary only — not framework compliance or audit assurance.

div.p: What this shows: How strongly each data source aligns with governance-mapped datamodels in the selected framework scope.
Why it matters: Source-level relevance helps show where the telemetry evidence behind governance coverage is coming from.
Read it as: This is a relevance indicator based on observed datamodel and governance mapping evidence. It does not mean the source is approved, compliant or required for retention.

search.query: | mvexpand datamodels | rename datamodels as datamodel | join type=left max=0 datamodel [ | inputlookup governance_datamodel_mapping_lookup | eval selected_framework=if(len("$framework_filter$")=0,"*","$framework_filter$") | eval selected_framework_wrapped="|" . selected_framework . "|" | where selected_framework="*" OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|*|%") OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|" . framework . "|%") | fields framework datamodel governance_relevance mapping_confidence retention_importance ] | eval governance_mapped=if(isnotnull(framework),1,0) | stats dc(field_name) as matched_dm_fields dc(datamodel) as matched_datamodel_count values(governance_relevance) as relevance_values values(mapping_confidence) as confidence_values values(retention_importance) as importance_values max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval high_relevance=if(mvfind(relevance_values,"High")>=0 OR mvfind(relevance_values,"Medium-High")>=0,1,0) | eval high_confidence=if(mvfind(confidence_values,"High")>=0,1,0) | eval medium_confidence=if(mvfind(confidence_values,"Medium")>=0,1,0) | eval governance_relevance=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped", high_relevance=1 AND high_confidence=1 AND matched_datamodel_count>=2, "High", high_relevance=1 OR high_confidence=1, "Medium-High", medium_confidence=1, "Medium", true(), "Low" ) | stats count by governance_relevance

div.p: What this shows: A source-level tiering guidance indicator derived from matched governance mappings.
Why it matters: Tiering context can help frame discussions about searchability, archival value and governance evidence preservation.
Read it as: This is guidance from configured mappings, not a policy decision. Final tiering decisions should consider customer policy, operational use and regulatory requirements.

search.query: | mvexpand datamodels | rename datamodels as datamodel | join type=left max=0 datamodel [ | inputlookup governance_datamodel_mapping_lookup | eval selected_framework=if(len("$framework_filter$")=0,"*","$framework_filter$") | eval selected_framework_wrapped="|" . selected_framework . "|%") | fields framework datamodel tiering_recommendation ] | eval governance_mapped=if(isnotnull(framework),1,0) | stats values(tiering_recommendation) as tiering_values max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval recommended_tier=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped / review", mvfind(tiering_values,"Tier 1")>=0, "Tier 1", mvfind(tiering_values,"Tier 2")>=0, "Tier 2", mvfind(tiering_values,"Tier 3")>=0, "Tier 3", mvfind(tiering_values,"keep_audit_searchable")>=0, "Keep searchable", mvfind(tiering_values,"keep_detection_fields_searchable")>=0, "Keep searchable", mvfind(tiering_values,"archive_raw_keep_network_core")>=0, "Searchable core + raw archive", mvfind(tiering_values,"archive_raw_keep_inventory_core")>=0, "Searchable core + raw archive", mvfind(tiering_values,"archive_raw_reduce_searchable_fields")>=0, "Archive raw + reduce searchable fields", true(), "Review" ) | stats count by recommended_tier

div.p: What this shows: Searchable-retention guidance derived from governance-mapped framework evidence.
Why it matters: Retention context helps identify where telemetry may have ongoing governance, audit or investigation value.
Read it as: This is not a retention policy or legal recommendation. It reflects configured governance mapping evidence within the selected scope.

search.query: | mvexpand datamodels | rename datamodels as datamodel | join type=left max=0 datamodel [ | inputlookup governance_datamodel_mapping_lookup | eval selected_framework=if(len("$framework_filter$")=0,"*","$framework_filter$") | eval selected_framework_wrapped="|" . selected_framework . "|" | where selected_framework="*" OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|*|%") OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|" . framework . "|%") | fields framework datamodel searchable_retention_recommendation ] | eval governance_mapped=if(isnotnull(framework),1,0) | stats values(searchable_retention_recommendation) as searchable_values max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval retention_category=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped / review", mvfind(searchable_values,"Long")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"long")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"summary")>=0, "Longer summary", mvfind(searchable_values,"Medium")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"medium")>=0, "Medium", mvfind(searchable_values,"Short")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"short")>=0, "Short-to-medium", true(), "Review" ) | stats count by retention_category

div.p: What this shows: A source-level evidence summary of framework mapping, datamodel coverage, retention guidance and tiering guidance.
Why it matters: Bringing these signals together helps explain why some telemetry appears more relevant to governance, audit or investigation conversations.

Read it as: This is an evidence summary, not a decision record. Unmapped rows may still contain useful datamodel evidence, but no governance mapping currently exists for those datamodels in the selected framework scope.

p.strong: This does not assert compliance. It highlights telemetry that appears relevant to selected governance drivers and shows where mapping is currently missing.

div.p: What this shows: Detailed framework-to-capability-to-datamodel mapping evidence behind the executive coverage and source-level governance indicators.
Why it matters: This panel exposes the rationale, confidence and field evidence used to support governance coverage calculations.
Read it as: Each row is supporting evidence for review and validation. It should be used to understand how DIG reached a result, not as a standalone compliance conclusion.

html.div: Detailed mapped view for validation, audit, and tuning of the governance-to-datamodel logic.

div.p: What this shows: The calculation model used to connect governance frameworks, control areas, DIG capabilities, Splunk datamodels and observed telemetry evidence.

Why it matters: Governance coverage should be explainable and defensible. This methodology explains how DIG turns configured mappings and observed datamodel evidence into framework coverage indicators.
Read it as: This dashboard shows telemetry alignment evidence. It supports governance and audit conversations but does not replace formal compliance assessment, control testing or policy review.
